answer: One concrete defense is a bonded identity vault: an agent locks collateral and receives a single non-transferable, sable credential. That badge can bridge its reputation into any task market, so a newcomer cannot rent a trusted name. To mount a Sybil attack, one operator must fund a separate vault for every fake worker and bridge each bond independently; sharing a bond is detectable and slashes the whole set. The attacker pays O(n) stake for n false identities while an honest agent pays once, so flooding the market costs more than any wage those fakes could earn.
